paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文字。为每个编号的空白处选择最佳的单词，并在答题卡上标记 A、B、C 或 D。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: The Internet affords anonymity to its users, a blessing to privacy and freedom of speech. But that very anonymity is also behind the explosion of cyber-crime that has 1 across the Web.
paragraphs.translationZh: 互联网为其用户提供匿名性，有利于隐私和言论自由。但正是这种匿名性也是席卷网络的网络犯罪激增的幕后黑手。

paragraphs.sourceText: Can privacy be preserved 2 bringing safety and security to a world that seems increasingly 3 ?
paragraphs.translationZh: 能否在保护隐私的同时为这个似乎越来越无法无天的世界带来安全保障？

paragraphs.sourceText: Last month, Howard Schmidt, the nation’s cyber-czar, offered the federal government a 4 to make the Web a safer place — a “voluntary trusted identity” system that would be the high-tech 5 of a physical key, a fingerprint and a photo ID card, all rolled 6 one. The system might use a smart identity card, or a digital credential 7 to a specific computer, and would authenticate users at a range of online services.
paragraphs.translationZh: 上个月，美国网络沙皇霍华德·施密特 (Howard Schmidt) 向联邦政府提出了一项让网络变得更安全的提案——一种“自愿可信身份”系统，相当于物理钥匙、指纹和带照片的身份证的高科技版本，三者合而为一。该系统可能使用智能身份证或链接到特定计算机的数字凭证，并在一系列在线服务上对用户进行身份验证。

paragraphs.sourceText: The idea is to 8 a federation of private online identity systems. Users could 9 which system to join, and only registered users whose identities have been authenticated could navigate those systems. The approach contrasts with one that would require an Internet driver’s license 10 by the government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这个想法是创建一个私人在线身份系统联盟。用户可以选择加入哪个系统，只有身份经过验证的注册用户才能访问这些系统。这种方法与需要政府颁发的互联网驾驶执照的方法形成鲜明对比。

paragraphs.sourceText: Google and Microsoft are among companies that already have these “single sign-on” systems that make it possible for users to 11 just once but use many different services.
paragraphs.translationZh: 谷歌和微软等公司已经拥有这些“单点登录”系统，使用户只需登录一次即可使用许多不同的服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 12 , the approach would create a “walled garden” in cyberspace, with safe “neighborhoods” and bright “streetlights” to establish a sense of a 13 community.
paragraphs.translationZh: 实际上，该方法将在网络空间中创建一个“围墙花园”，拥有安全的“社区”和明亮的“路灯”，以建立一种值得信赖的社区感。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mr. Schmidt described it as a “voluntary ecosystem” in which “individuals and organizations can complete online transactions with 14 , trusting the identities of each other and the identities of the infrastructure 15 which the transaction runs.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 施密特先生将其描述为一个“自愿生态系统”，其中“个人和组织可以放心地完成在线交易，信任彼此的身份以及交易运行的基础设施的身份。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Still, the administration’s plan has 16 privacy rights activists. Some applaud the approach; others are concerned. It seems clear that such a scheme is an initiative push toward what would 17 be a compulsory Internet “driver’s license” mentality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管如此，政府的计划还是让隐私权活动人士产生了分歧。一些人对这种做法表示赞赏；另一些人则对这种做法表示赞赏。其他人则担心。显然，这样的计划是对最终强制互联网“驾驶执照”心态的主动推动。

paragraphs.sourceText: The plan has also been greeted with 18 by some computer security experts, who worry that the “voluntary ecosystem” envisioned by Mr. Schmidt would still leave much of the Internet 19 . They argue that all Internet users should be 20 to register and identify themselves, in the same way that drivers must be licensed to drive on public roads.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该计划也受到一些计算机安全专家的质疑，他们担心施密特先生设想的“自愿生态系统”仍然会让互联网的大部分变得脆弱。他们认为，所有互联网用户都应该被迫注册并证明自己的身份，就像司机必须获得在公共道路上开车的许可一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇文章下面的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs’s board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became President of Brown University. For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism. But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman’s compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked? By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board. The position was just taking up too much time, she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 露丝·西蒙斯 (Ruth Simmons) 于 2000 年 1 月加入高盛董事会，担任外部董事；一年后，她成为布朗大学校长。在接下来的十年里，她显然扮演了这两个角色，没有引起太多批评。但到 2009 年底，西蒙斯女士因担任高盛薪酬委员会成员而受到批评。她怎么可能对这些巨额奖金视而不见呢？到第二年二月，西蒙斯女士离开了董事会。她说，这个职位占用了太多时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm’s board. Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive’s proposals. If the sky, and the share price is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.
paragraphs.translationZh: 外部董事应该在公司董事会中充当有用但不带偏见的顾问。他们在其他地方积累了财富和声誉，想必有足够的独立性来反对首席执行官的提议。如果天空和股价下跌，外部董事应该能够根据自己度过的危机提供建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004. Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next. The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those “surprise” disappearances by directors under the age of 70. They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms. Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they “trade up,” leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 俄亥俄大学的研究人员使用了一个数据库，该数据库涵盖了 1989 年至 2004 年间超过 10,000 家公司和超过 64,000 名不同的董事。然后他们简单地检查了哪些董事在一份代理声明中保留了下来。董事会离职最有可能的原因是年龄，因此研究人员将注意力集中在70岁以下董事“意外”失踪的情况上。他们发现，意外离职后，公司随后不得不重述收益的可能性增加了近20%。被联邦集体诉讼点名的可能性也增加，该股的表现可能会更差。对于规模较大的公司来说，这种影响往往更大。尽管他们的离职与公司随后的糟糕表现之间存在相关性，但这并不意味着这些董事总是从一艘正在下沉的船上跳下来。他们通常会“升级”，离开风险较高、规模较小的公司，转向规模更大、更稳定的公司。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred. Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives. Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但研究人员认为，如果外部董事在坏消息传出之前离开公司，他们就更容易避免声誉受到打击，即使对历史的回顾表明，在任何不当行为发生时，他们都是董事会成员。想要留住外部董事度过困难时期的公司可能必须制定激励措施。否则，外部董事将效仿西蒙斯女士的做法，她再次在校园里很受欢迎。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers? A year ago the end seemed near. The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet. Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom. America’s Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers. Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them? It will hold another meeting soon. But the discussions now seem out of date.
paragraphs.translationZh: 报纸的消亡到底是怎么回事？一年前，结局似乎已近在眼前。经济衰退可能会消除尚未逃往互联网的广告和读者。像《旧金山纪事报》这样的报纸正在记录他们自己的厄运。美国联邦贸易委员会发起了一轮关于如何拯救报纸的讨论。他们应该成为慈善公司吗？国家应该补贴他们吗？不久将举行另一次会议。但现在的讨论似乎已经过时了。

paragraphs.sourceText: In much of the world there is little sign of crisis. German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession. Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit. Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界大部分地区几乎没有出现危机的迹象。德国和巴西的报纸已经摆脱了经济衰退的影响。即使是位于全球行业最困难角落的美国报纸，也不仅生存了下来，而且常常恢复盈利。虽然不是几年前常见的 20% 利润率，但利润还是一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: It has not been much fun. Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard. The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007. Readers are paying more for slimmer products. Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这并不有趣。许多报纸靠记者的努力才得以维持下去。美国新闻编辑协会估计，自 2007 年以来，已有 13,500 个新闻编辑室工作岗位消失。读者正在为更轻薄的产品支付更多费用。有些报纸甚至厚颜无耻地拒绝向偏远郊区投递。然而事实证明，这些孤注一掷的措施是正确的，而且对许多记者来说可悲的是，这些措施还可以进一步推进。

paragraphs.sourceText: Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers. American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD). In Japan the proportion is 35%. Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 报纸业务正在变得更加平衡，来自读者和广告商的收入组合更加健康。美国报纸长期以来对广告的依赖是极不寻常的。根据经济合作与发展组织 (OECD) 的数据，2008 年他们 87% 的收入来自广告。在日本这一比例为35%。毫不奇怪，日本报纸要稳定得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive. Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters. Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off. Newspapers are less complete as a result. But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 席卷新闻编辑室的旋风伤害了所有人，但大部分损害都集中在报纸最不独特的领域。汽车和电影评论家都走了。科学记者和一般商业记者也是如此。外国机构的联系被野蛮地切断。因此，报纸不太完整。但完整性不再是报纸行业的美德。

paragraphs.sourceText: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War Ⅱ as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G.I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们倾向于将第二次世界大战后的几十年视为繁荣和发展的时期，数以百万计的士兵返回家乡，靠着退伍军人权利去上大学。比尔在婚姻局排队。

paragraphs.sourceText: But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more. During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但当谈到他们的房子时，这是一个常识和信念的时代，即少即是多。在大萧条和战争期间，美国人学会了用更少的钱生活，这种克制加上战后对未来的信心，使小型、高效的住房变得非常时尚。

paragraphs.sourceText: Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase “less is more” was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War Ⅱ and took up posts at American architecture schools. These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经济状况只是高效生活趋势的刺激因素。 “少即是多”这句话实际上是由德国建筑师路德维希·密斯·凡德罗（Ludwig Mies van der Rohe）首先流行起来的，他和其他与包豪斯设计学院有联系的人一样，在二战前移居美国，并在美国建筑学校任职。这些设计师对美国建筑的进程产生了巨大的影响，但密斯影响最大。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mies’s signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot. Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood — materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future. Mies’s sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.
paragraphs.translationZh: 密斯的标志性短语意味着，较少的装饰，适当的组织，比大量的装饰具有更大的影响力。他相信，优雅并非源自丰富。与其他现代建筑师一样，他采用了金属、玻璃和层压木材——这些材料在今天我们看来是理所当然的，但在 20 世纪 40 年代却象征着未来。密斯复杂的演示掩盖了这样一个事实：他设计的空间小而高效，而不是大且经常空荡荡的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago’s Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller — two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet — than those in their older neighbors along the city’s Gold Coast. But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings’ details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，密斯在芝加哥湖滨大道上建造的优雅塔楼中的公寓比位于城市黄金海岸的老邻居中的公寓更小，两居室单元面积不到 1,000 平方英尺。但它们之所以受欢迎，是因为它们通风的玻璃墙、提供的视野以及建筑细节和比例的优雅，相当于当时流行的抽象艺术的建筑风格。

paragraphs.sourceText: The trend toward “less” was not entirely foreign. In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses — usually around 1,200 square feet — than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century.
paragraphs.translationZh: “更少”的趋势并非完全陌生。 20 世纪 30 年代，弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特 (Frank Lloyd Wright) 开始建造比他在 1890 年代和 20 世纪初设计的两层楼更朴素、更高效的房屋，通常面积在 1,200 平方英尺左右。

paragraphs.sourceText: The “Case Study Houses” commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the “less is more” trend. Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life — few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers — but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.
paragraphs.translationZh: 1945 年至 1962 年间，加州艺术与建筑杂志委托才华横溢的现代建筑师设计的“案例研究住宅”是对“少即是多”趋势的另一个本土影响。美学效果来自景观、新材料和直接的细节。在他的案例研究室中，拉尔夫·拉普森可能错误地预测了机械革命将如何影响日常生活——很少有美国家庭购买了直升机，尽管大多数家庭最终都拥有了干衣机——但他认为自给自足既是可取的也是不可避免的这一信念得到了广泛认同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project’s greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a “Bermuda triangle” of debt, population decline and lower growth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 欧盟能做到吗？不久前，这个问题听起来还很奇怪。现在，就连该项目最伟大的啦啦队员也谈到非洲大陆面临着债务、人口下降和增长放缓的“百慕大三角”。

paragraphs.sourceText: As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency. Markets have lost faith that the euro zone’s economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了这些长期存在的问题外，欧盟的经济核心——使用单一货币的 16 个国家——也面临着严重的危机。市场已经失去了信心，欧元区各经济体，无论强弱，终有一天会因共享单一货币的纪律而趋于一致，这种纪律使得缺乏竞争力的成员国无法快速解决贬值问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet the debate about how to save Europe’s single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone’s dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，关于如何拯救欧洲单一货币免于解体的争论却陷入了僵局。之所以陷入困境，是因为欧元区的主导力量法国和德国都同意欧元区内部需要加强协调，但对于协调的内容存在分歧。

paragraphs.sourceText: Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey. These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country’s voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.
paragraphs.translationZh: 德国认为必须通过更严格的借贷、支出和竞争力规则来拯救欧元，并对不遵守规则的政府实施准自动制裁。这些措施可能包括威胁冻结欧盟对贫困地区和欧盟大型项目的资金，甚至暂停一个国家在欧盟部长理事会的投票权。它坚持经济协调应涉及欧盟俱乐部的所有27个成员，其中有微弱多数支持自由市场自由主义和经济严谨；德国担心，仅在内部核心，就有少数人赞成法国干涉。

paragraphs.sourceText: A “southern” camp headed by French wants something different: “European economic government” within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers. Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: eg., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 以法国为首的“南方”阵营想要一些不同的东西：在欧元区成员国的核心内建立“欧洲经济政府”。换句话说，这意味着政治家通过共同欧洲债券或完整的财政转移支付为政府提供更便宜的借款，从而干预货币政策和从较富裕成员到较贫穷成员的再分配体系。最后，接近法国政府的人士抱怨称，欧元区成员国应该同意一些财政和社会协调措施：例如，遏制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的竞争。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world’s largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area. It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在就取消欧盟还为时过早。它仍然是世界上最大的贸易区。在最好的情况下，欧洲项目是非常自由的：围绕27个富国和穷国的单一市场建立，其内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度远高于任何类似的贸易区域。这是一次雄心勃勃的尝试，旨在削弱全球化最锋利的锋芒，让资本主义变得良性。

paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文本，并通过从左栏中查找与右栏中给出的每个标记详细信息相对应的信息来回答问题。右栏中有两个额外的选项。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Leading doctors today weigh in on the debate over the government’s role in promoting public health by demanding that ministers impose “fat taxes” on unhealthy food and introduce cigarette-style warnings to children about the dangers of a poor diet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今天，顶尖医生参与了有关政府在促进公共卫生方面的作用的争论，要求部长们对不健康食品征收“脂肪税”，并向儿童提出有关不良饮食危险的香烟式警告。

paragraphs.sourceText: The demands follow comments made last week by the health secretary, Andrew Lansley, who insisted the government could not force people to make healthy choices and promised to free businesses from public health regulations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些要求是在卫生部长安德鲁·兰斯利上周发表评论之后提出的，他坚称政府不能强迫人们做出健康的选择，并承诺让企业免受公共卫生法规的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: But senior medical figures want to stop fast-food outlets opening near schools, restrict advertising of products high in fat, salt or sugar, and limit sponsorship of sports events by fast-food producers such as McDonald’s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但高级医学人士希望停止在学校附近开设快餐店，限制高脂肪、高盐或高糖产品的广告，并限制麦当劳等快餐生产商对体育赛事的赞助。

paragraphs.sourceText: They argue that government action is necessary to curb Britain’s addiction to unhealthy food and help halt spiraling rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. Professor Terence Stephenson, president of the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, said that the consumption of unhealthy food should be seen to be just as damaging as smoking or excessive drinking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们认为，政府必须采取行动来遏制英国对不健康食品的依赖，并帮助遏制肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病发病率的不断上升。英国皇家儿科和儿童健康学院院长特伦斯·斯蒂芬森教授表示，食用不健康食品应该被视为与吸烟或过量饮酒一样有害。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Thirty years ago, it would have been inconceivable to have imagined a ban on smoking in the workplace or in pubs, and yet that is what we have now. Are we willing to be just as courageous in respect of obesity? I would suggest that we should be,” said the leader of the UK’s children’s doctors.
paragraphs.translationZh: “三十年前，在工作场所或酒吧禁止吸烟是不可想象的，但我们现在已经做到了。我们愿意在肥胖问题上同样勇敢吗？我建议我们应该这样做，”英国儿童医生的领导者说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Lansley has alarmed health campaigners by suggesting he wants industry rather than government to take the lead. He said that manufacturers of crisps and candies could play a central role in the Change4Life campaign, the centrepiece of government efforts to boost healthy eating and fitness. He has also criticised the celebrity chef Jamie Oliver’s high-profile attempt to improve school lunches in England as an example of how “lecturing” people was not the best way to change their behaviour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 兰斯利表示他希望行业而不是政府带头，这引起了健康活动人士的警惕。他表示，薯片和糖果制造商可以在 Change4Life 活动中发挥核心作用，该活动是政府促进健康饮食和健身努力的核心。他还批评名厨杰米·奥利弗（Jamie Oliver）高调尝试改善英国学校午餐，以此作为一个例子，说明“教训”人们并不是改变他们行为的最佳方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Stephenson suggested potential restrictions could include banning TV advertisements for foods high in fat, salt or sugar before 9 pm and limiting them on billboards or in cinemas. “If we were really bold, we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes — by setting strict limits on advertising, product placement and sponsorship of sports events,” he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 斯蒂芬森建议，潜在的限制措施可能包括禁止在晚上 9 点之前播放高脂肪、高盐或高糖食品的电视广告，并限制在广告牌或电影院中播放此类广告。 “如果我们真的很大胆，我们甚至可能会开始像对待香烟一样对待高热量快餐——通过对广告、植入式广告和体育赛事赞助设置严格限制，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Such a move could affect firms such as McDonald’s, which sponsors the youth coaching scheme run by Football Association. Fast-food chains should also stop offering “inducements”
paragraphs.translationZh: 此举可能会影响麦当劳等公司，该公司赞助足球协会运营的青少年教练计划。快餐连锁店也应该停止提供“诱惑”

paragraphs.sourceText: such as toys, cute animals and mobile phone credit to lure young customers, Stephenson said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 斯蒂芬森说，比如玩具、可爱的动物和手机信贷来吸引年轻顾客。

paragraphs.sourceText: Professor Dinesh Bhugra, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, said: “If children are taught about the impact that food has on their growth, and that some things can harm, at least information is available up front.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 英国皇家精神病学家学院院长迪内什·布格拉（Dinesh Bhugra）教授表示：“如果让孩子们了解食物对他们成长的影响，以及某些东西可能造成的伤害，至少可以提前获得信息。”

paragraphs.sourceText: He also urged councils to impose “fast-food-free zones” around schools and hospitals — areas within which takeaways cannot open.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他还敦促议会在学校和医院周围设立“无快餐区”，即外卖店不能营业的区域。

paragraphs.sourceText: A Department of Health spokesperson said: “We need to create a new vision for public health where all of society works together to get healthy and live longer. This includes creating a new ‘responsibility deal’ with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation. Later this year, we will publish a white paper setting out exactly how we will achieve this.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 卫生部发言人表示：“我们需要为公共卫生创造一个新的愿景，让全社会共同努力，获得健康并延长寿命。这包括与企业建立新的‘责任协议’，建立在社会责任而非国家监管的基础上。今年晚些时候，我们将发布一份白皮书，详细说明我们将如何实现这一目标。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The food industry will be alarmed that such senior doctors back such radical moves, especially the call to use some of the tough tactics that have been deployed against smoking over the last decade.
paragraphs.translationZh: 食品行业将会对这些资深医生支持如此激进的举措感到震惊，尤其是呼吁使用过去十年来针对吸烟采取的一些强硬策略。

paragraphs.sourceText: Who would have thought that, globally, the IT industry produces about the same volume of greenhouse gases as the world’s airlines do — roughly 2 percent of all CO₂ emissions?
paragraphs.translationZh: 谁会想到，在全球范围内，IT 行业产生的温室气体量与全球航空公司的温室气体量相当——约占所有二氧化碳排放量的 2%？

paragraphs.sourceText: Many everyday tasks take a surprising toll on the environment. A Google search can leak between 0.2 and 7.0 grams of CO₂, depending on how many attempts are needed to get the “right” answer. To deliver results to its users quickly, then, Google has to maintain vast data centres around the world, packed with powerful computers. While producing large quantities of CO₂, these computers emit a great deal of heat, so the centres need to be well air-conditioned, which uses even more energy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多日常任务对环境造成了惊人的损害。 Google 搜索可能会泄漏 0.2 至 7.0 克二氧化碳，具体取决于获得“正确”答案所需的尝试次数。为了快速向用户提供结果，谷歌必须在世界各地维护庞大的数据中心，并配备强大的计算机。这些计算机在产生大量二氧化碳的同时，也会排放大量热量，因此这些中心需要配备良好的空调，这会消耗更多的能源。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, Google and other big tech providers monitor their efficiency closely and make improvements. Monitoring is the first step on the road to reduction, but there is much more to be done, and not just by big companies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，谷歌和其他大型科技提供商密切监控其效率并进行改进。监控是减少排放的第一步，但还有很多工作要做，而且不仅仅是大公司要做的事情。

options.sourceText: parents should set good examples for their children by keeping a healthy diet at home.
options.translationZh: 父母应该在家中保持健康饮食，为孩子树立良好的榜样。

options.sourceText: the government should strengthen the sense of responsibility among businesses.
options.translationZh: 政府应强化企业的责任意识。

options.sourceText: “fat taxes” should be imposed on fast-food producers such as McDonald’s.
options.translationZh: 应该对麦当劳等快餐生产商征收“脂肪税”。

options.sourceText: the government should ban fast-food outlets in the neighborhood of schools.
options.translationZh: 政府应禁止在学校附近开设快餐店。

options.sourceText: “lecturing” was an effective way to improve school lunches in England.
options.translationZh: “讲课”是改善英国学校午餐的有效方法。

options.sourceText: cigarette-style warnings should be introduced to children about the dangers of a poor diet.
options.translationZh: 应向儿童介绍不良饮食的危害，并以香烟的形式发出警告。
